environmentName.$comment: The exact string spec/validate.py declares as ENVIRONMENT_NAME_PATTERN, which scripts/tests/test_spec_validate.py asserts. repo-config/configure.sh resolves the name with select(.name == $n) and then percent-encodes it into one path segment. Printable ASCII, per GOVERNANCE.md 'Documentation Style Conventions' and its 'Character Set' rule, rather than any non-blank string, and a grammar rather than a padding test because str.strip() does not remove a zero-width space, so a name ending in one survives a padding test and then matches no live environment.

groundTruthBranch.$comment: The exact string spec/validate.py declares as GROUND_TRUTH_BRANCH_PATTERN, which scripts/tests/test_spec_validate.py asserts. The value is concatenated raw into a request path and a `?ref=` query value, so it admits only the characters that are both unreserved in RFC 3986 and legal in a git ref name, plus `/`, and it refuses `..`, which the live API resolves as a traversal. One $def rather than two literals so that neither key can drift from the other, and spec/validate.py checks both keys against it, since a pattern here on a key the gate did not check would make this schema the stricter of the two.

allOf.$comment: An operational repo must declare its line endings (release repos use the fleet LF default).
An excluded repo records the deliberate decision that put it out of audit scope, not just the fact.

A cataloged repo is the set spec/audit.py audits, and there an absent hasDevelop is coerced to false and compared against the live branch rather than read as undeclared, so omitting it asserts that the repo has no develop branch. spec/validate.py requires it on the same status.

name.$comment: Length alone here, and the field's real shape is stated by spec/validate.py, which requires the name to equal its own url's repo segment. JSON Schema cannot compare two sibling properties, so the rule can only live in the gate. Agreement is what gives the name a grammar: the url is held to GitHub's own repository-name characters, so a name equal to that segment carries nothing invisible without a pattern of its own.

description.$comment: Deliberately looser than spec/validate.py's description_errors(), which is the gate: this refuses only a line break and a leading or trailing ASCII space, both of which that function also refuses. It does not express the link-free rule, the full leading/trailing whitespace rule, or a character set, because a description may legitimately carry a tier-2 or tier-3 non-ASCII character (a degree sign, a unit symbol) that no portable positive grammar enumerates. A pattern here that refused something the gate accepts would leave an editor rejecting a valid registry, so where the two differ this one is the permissive side by design. `(?![\s\S])` rather than `$`, since `$` also matches before a trailing newline in Python's engine and would admit a value description_errors() refuses.

exclusionReason.$comment: Length alone, with no pattern: the blank-value rule is spec/validate.py's, which is the gate, and stating it here needed `\S`, whose set differs between Python and ECMA-262. That divergence had an editor refusing a value the gate accepts, the direction an advisory schema must never be wrong in.

items.$comment: The exact string spec/validate.py declares as SECRET_NAME_PATTERN, which scripts/tests/test_spec_validate.py asserts. A name here is resolved against the repository actions store by an exact comparison, so a padded element reports as missing on every run while the name it was meant to be goes unrequired. The shape a name must have to resolve against the actions store spec/audit.py compares it to by exact set difference, and it is portable between Python re and ECMA-262 for the reason the grammars above give. Upper case because a stored name is upper case, so a lower-case declaration matches none and reports missing on every run while the name it meant reports as claimed by no mechanism. The reserved GITHUB_ prefix because GitHub refuses to store such a name at all, so a repo declaring one collects a finding nothing it can do retires.

allOf.$comment: A custom policy names the exact branch set it allows, and none names no set because it admits every ref. GitHub's third form, protected branches only, is not offered: it counts classic branch protection, which this fleet removes in favor of rulesets, so declaring it would assert a gate that does not exist.

items.$comment: The name and branches patterns this object reaches are the exact strings spec/validate.py declares as ENVIRONMENT_NAME_PATTERN and DEPLOYMENT_BRANCH_PATTERN, and scripts/tests/test_spec_validate.py fails if they ever stop being identical. Both are written in what Python re and ECMA-262 share, so the gate and an editor resolving this schema refuse the same values: `(?![\s\S])` rather than `$`, which is end-of-string in only one of the two, and literal ASCII ranges rather than `\s` or `\S`, which name a different set in each. That agreement is what makes an editor-side copy safe, and an earlier attempt was reverted in #1504 for leaving an editor refusing what the gate allowed.

Length alone, no pattern: a note is prose. spec/validate.py, which is the gate, also refuses a note that is only whitespace, and stating that here needed a character set this schema keeps out for the reason exclusionReason gives. The type is what matters, since spec/audit.py slices each note and runs a regex over it, so a non-string element raises mid-run rather than reporting.
